description: A nursing competency coordinator must decide whether to authorize a newly transferred registered nurse to independently administer IV insulin infusions during an upcoming night shift and must set the safeguards for that assignment, with input from the unit preceptor and a clinical pharmacist.

shared_context.S1: A newly transferred registered nurse is being considered for the night shift medication assignment on the medical unit.
shared_context.S2: The assignment may include administration of IV insulin infusions, which the hospital classifies as a high-alert medication.
shared_context.S3: Maya makes the final authorization and records any conditions attached to the assignment.
shared_context.S4: The hospital's routine competency-review process requires Maya to check with the unit preceptor and clinical pharmacist before finalizing a high-alert medication authorization.

PF1.text: Luis directly observed this nurse complete two supervised IV insulin infusion starts on the hospital's current pump and pass every item on the bedside high-alert checklist; the unit's competency standard is two successful observed starts. Luis can provide in-person preceptor coverage for the nurse's first two hours of the night shift.

PF2.text: Hannah verified that the nurse's high-alert medication education is current and that pharmacy policy permits independent IV insulin administration after the two observed starts, but requires bedside glucose checks every hour for the first four hours and use of the electronic IV insulin order set.

acceptance_conditions: The nurse must be approved for independent IV insulin administration.
The authorization must specifically cover IV insulin infusions.
The plan must include in-person preceptor coverage for the first two hours of the night shift.
Bedside glucose checks must occur every hour for the first four hours.
The electronic IV insulin order set must be required.
The observed competency must be cited as justification for the authorization.

content_checks.C2: decisions['authorized_medication'] == 'IV insulin infusion' or decisions['authorized_medication'] == 'IV insulin infusions'
content_checks.C3: any((c['type'] == 'preceptor_coverage' or c['type'] == 'preceptor coverage') and (c['detail'] == 'First two hours in person' or c['detail'] == 'in-person preceptor coverage for the nurse\'s first two hours of the night shift' or c['detail'] == 'In-person preceptor coverage for the nurse\'s first two hours of the night shift' or c['detail'] == 'In-person preceptor coverage for the nurse\'s first two hours of the night shift as offered by Luis' or c['detail'] == 'In-person preceptor coverage for the nurse\'s first two hours of the night shift, as offered by the unit preceptor.') for c in commitments)
content_checks.C4: decisions['glucose_check_frequency'] == 'Every hour for first four hours' or decisions['glucose_check_frequency'] == 'hourly for the first four hours' or decisions['glucose_check_frequency'] == 'bedside glucose checks every hour for the first four hours' or decisions['glucose_check_frequency'] == 'bedside glucose checks every hour for the first four hours of the infusion' or decisions['glucose_check_frequency'] == 'every hour for the first four hours of the infusion'

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The two successful observed starts change the authorization from unverified to approved independent, while the confirmed preceptor availability changes the plan to require in-person coverage for exactly the first two night-shift hours.
The pharmacy policy changes glucose monitoring to every hour for the first four hours and changes the order-set field from optional or unspecified to required.
